nodes.text: For we warn you in advance to be on your guard, lest the demons whom we have been accusing deceive you and turn you away from reading and understanding what we say at all (for they strive to have you as slaves and servants, and sometimes through appearances in dreams, sometimes again through magical tricks, they subdue all who make no effort at all for their own salvation), just as we too, after being persuaded by the Word, have withdrawn from them, and follow the only unbegotten God through his Son: we who formerly delighted in fornication now embrace self-control alone; we who also used magical arts have now dedicated ourselves to the good and unbegotten God; we who valued the means of gaining money and possessions above everything now bring what we have into a common stock and share with everyone in need; we who hated and killed one another, and because of [their] customs would not share a hearth with those not of our own race, now, after the appearance of Christ, live at one table, and pray for our enemies, and try to persuade those who hate us unjustly, so that those who live according to the good precepts of Christ may have good hope of obtaining with us the same things from God, the master of all. And so that we may not seem to be using sophistry on you, we have thought it well, before the proof, to recall a few of the teachings given by Christ himself; and let it be your task, as powerful kings, to examine whether we have truly been taught and do teach these things. Short and concise were the sayings that came from him; for he was no sophist, but his word was the power of God.

For look at the end of each of the kings who have been, how they died the death common to all; and if this led to insensibility, it would be a godsend to all the unjust. But since sensation remains for all who have ever lived, and eternal punishment is laid up, do not neglect to be persuaded and to believe that these things are true. For let necromancies, and the inspections made through uncorrupted boys, and the summoning of human souls, and those whom the magicians call dream-senders and attendant spirits, and the things done by those who know these arts, persuade you that even after death souls are in a state of sensation; and [so too] the men who are seized and thrown about by the souls of the dead, whom everyone calls demon-possessed and mad; and what you call the oracles of Amphilochus and Dodona and Pytho, and all others of that kind; and the teachings of the writers, Empedocles and Pythagoras, Plato and Socrates, and the pit in Homer, and the descent of Odysseus to inspect these things, and [the teachings] of those who have said the same as they. Accept us at least as you accept them, since we believe in God not less than they, but more, we who expect to receive back our own bodies even when they are dead and cast into the earth, saying that nothing is impossible for God.

Third, that even after Christ's ascent into heaven the demons put forward certain men who said that they themselves were gods, who were not only not persecuted by you but were even thought worthy of honours. [They put forward] a certain Simon, a Samaritan, from a village called Gitta, who in the time of Claudius Caesar, through the art of the demons at work [in him], performed magical powers in your imperial city of Rome and was considered a god, and has been honoured by you with a statue as a god; this statue has been set up on the river Tiber between the two bridges, bearing this Latin inscription: SIMONI DEO SANCTO [To Simon the holy god]. And almost all the Samaritans, and a few also among other nations, acknowledge him as the first god and worship him; and a certain Helen, who went about with him at that time and had earlier stood in a brothel, they call the first Thought that came from him. And we know that a certain Menander, also a Samaritan, from the village of Capparetaea, who became a disciple of Simon, was likewise driven by the demons, and was in Antioch, deceived many through magic art; he even persuaded his followers that they would not die; and even now there are some from his [school] who profess this. And a certain Marcion of Pontus, who is even now still teaching those who are persuaded by him to believe in some other god greater than the creator; who, among every race of men, with the help of the demons, has made many speak blasphemies and deny that the maker of this universe is God, and profess that another, as being greater, has done greater things than he. All who start from these, as we said, are called Christians, just as those among the philosophers who do not share the same doctrines still have in common the name of philosophy that is applied to them. Whether they also do those infamous deeds that are told of, the overturning of the lamp, and unrestrained intercourse, and the eating of human flesh, we do not know; but that they are not persecuted or put to death by you, at least for their doctrines, we do know. We also have a treatise composed against all the heresies that have arisen, which, if you wish to read it, we will give [you].

But lest anyone should object to us, What prevents the one whom we call Christ, being a man born of men, from having done the powers we speak of by magic art, and from having seemed for this reason to be the son of God? we will now make our proof, not trusting those who [merely] assert, but of necessity believing those who prophesied [things] before they happened, because we see with our own eyes things that have happened and are happening as they were prophesied; and this, we think, will appear to you too the greatest and truest proof.
